s1.syndrome_frame: Systemic infection with multi-organ involvement and sepsis in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Acute hypoxic respiratory failure and septic shock
key_facts: Patient has HIV/AIDS with CD4 count <20 cells/µL
Patient has a history of intravenous drug use
Patient has active tobacco dependence
Patient reported one month of poor appetite and weight loss
Patient reported subjective fevers
Patient had diarrhea without abdominal pain, vomiting, cough, or dyspnea
Patient was febrile (39.4 °C) and hypotensive (91/60 mmHg)
Patient had leukocytosis (31 151/µL) and hyponatremia (Na 121 mEq/L)
Chest radiograph was clear initially
Abdominal ultrasound revealed hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, and enlarged peripancreatic lymph nodes
Patient developed acute hypoxic respiratory failure and septic shock
Blood cultures remained negative
Lumbar puncture demonstrated an opening pressure of 35 cm H₂O and 1825 RBCs/dL

shortlist.label: Disseminated tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with systemic infection and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Opportunistic infection common in HIV/AIDS patients with low CD4 count

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Common opportunistic infection in immunocompromised patients

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fungal infection that can cause systemic illness in immunocompromised patients

shortlist.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
shortlist.why_kept: Common bacterial infection in immunocompromised patients, especially those with HIV/AIDS

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of weight loss, fever, and night sweats, along with the findings of hepatosplenomegaly and ascites on abdominal ultrasound, are consistent with disseminated tuberculosis, particularly in the context of a severely immunocompromised patient with HIV/AIDS and a history of intravenous drug use.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: Bronchoalveolar lavage was negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii cultures

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
rejected.why: No specific evidence of CMV infection, such as positive cultures or PCR, is mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: The presence of 1825 RBCs/dL in the lumbar puncture is not typical for cryptococcal meningitis, which usually presents with elevated intracranial pressure and low glucose in the CSF

rejected.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
rejected.why: While possible in an immunocompromised patient, the clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not specifically point towards MAC infection as the primary diagnosis
